title: Meroitic Script
summary: Kush's scribes created a script for the Meroitic language in the 3rd century BCE, in two forms: a common cursive and a rarer hieroglyphic. Each was alphasyllabic with twenty-three signs. The first datable inscription names King Arnekhamani, about 220 BCE. Use ended in the 4th century CE.

uncertainty.note: Sources give only the 3rd century BC (early 3rd century for the cursive); the first datable inscription is put at 220 BC. Another site (Omniglot, not cited) gives c. 315 BC, so the emergence date is uncertain.

when.display: 3rd century BCE (first datable inscription c. 220 BCE)

where.modern_name: Meroe, River Nile State, Sudan (proxy pin: UNESCO Meroe 1 component, not a find spot of the script's invention)

importance.justification: Writing system of the Kingdom of Kush that replaced Egyptian for royal inscriptions.
